title: One verified compiled, fresh-bound routine on jev-use fill->submit vs ordinary and guarded callers (live TypeSafe), with all six #93 gates

source.merged: trycua/cua PR 4316 head a0bca744067d04f05904319d3d919be30c336556 (git merge --no-ff, conflict-free)
source.rust_tree_check: git diff --quiet 229b65b2849c3a595ddbc85200d7181b18bd2e47 031ee5f58 -- libs/cua-driver/rust succeeds (recorded in every phase validity.json)

shakedown_disclosure.note: Feasibility/harness shakedown ran BEFORE this file was frozen, with the mock provider only (0 provider requests). None of it is analysed as a measured trial. Raw kept under raw/shakedown/.
observed: set_agent_cursor_enabled is scoped to a session label: without `session` it lands on the implicit mcp-* session and run.py's jev-python-* label keeps feedback ON (smoke1 T~3.2 s in all arms). Fixed in the launcher: {enabled:false, session:<label>} before the first call of each Driver label (smoke2 T~186-211 ms).

N4a: the Driver's dom_event browser_click ACCEPTS a ref whose DOM node the page replaced after the snapshot (effect=unverifiable, no submit landed). The unmodified run.py path behaves the same (N4a_ord shakedown), and then re-dispatches Submit on a fresh ref after its 20x100 ms poll.

N4b: a ref from a superseded snapshot namespace is refused as effect=refused / browser_ref_stale with isError=false, so a caller must treat effect=refused as a refusal (run.py's Driver.call does not).
N5: the old target id is refused in a replacement session label (code authorization_host_failed); browser_prepare {pid} + get_browser_state {pid, window_id} rebinds the same browser.

Trusted (non-dom_event) browser_click is refused on this Linux standalone window (browser_input_trust_unavailable), so dom_event is the only background route; the artifact keeps the route the learning trace used.

hypothesis: A compiled routine whose artifact stores only logical targets, parameters, dependencies, preconditions, the expected outcome and fallback points, verified on a clean reset before admission and freshly bound before every mutation, removes both provider decisions on warm replay. It is faster than guarded completion (B, 1 decision) and the ordinary caller (A, 2 decisions), with paired CIs excluding 0, while all six #93 gates hold.

phases.P1_learning: 1 ordinary LIVE run (arm A config) with receipts; G1 = independently verified (journal applied==1 and /state.submitted==token) with exactly 2 TypeSafe decisions
phases.P2_compile: compile_trace(receipts) -> artifact; compile_ms timed in process; authority check must be empty
phases.P3_admission: fresh fixture (clean reset), fresh Driver+Chrome, compiled replay with fresh binding and NO fallback, 0 provider requests; the independent journal must verify BEFORE admission. Failure => KILL
phases.P4_warm: 20 rounds x {A,B,C}; per-round order rotates ABC,BCA,CAB,ACB,CBA,BAC,...; fresh Driver, Chrome, fixture and unique token per trial; EXCLUSIVE quiet-lane lock; loadavg at spawn and exit of every trial; every trial kept
phases.P5_gate4_negatives: in-process compiled replay with the MOCK chooser as fallback, untimed, SHARED quiet lock in blocks of <=10 trials, 3 reps each: N1 Submit renamed 'Send'; N2 Submit missing; N3 duplicate Submit; N4a page replaces the Submit node between bind and dispatch (no new snapshot); N4b a superseding snapshot is taken between bind and dispatch; N5 Driver session label replaced between steps (all target/tab/ref capabilities invalid; old-target probe must be refused; rebind via browser_prepare{pid}+get_browser_state{pid,window_id}); N6 typing opens a modal <dialog> over the form; N7 field prefilled with a different value; N8 artifact invoked on the issue24 toggle->confirm page (commit 5474aa31f, verbatim). Comparator N4a_ord: same re-render injection before the unmodified run.py's first browser_click (mock), 3 reps
phases.P6_gate5_reconcile: in-process compiled replay; acknowledgement loss injected on the compiled Submit at the seam between ClientSession and the SDK stdio streams (harness/fault_transport.py copied verbatim from R2-05 @ 236e37e01). Rows x5: applied_ack_lost (Driver response held until the target journal shows applied, dropped, EOF); delayed_after_first_unchanged_read (journal holds the first submit until one caller /state read returned unchanged after receipt; response held until received, dropped, EOF). Extra control row x3: withheld_unresolved (effect held until the caller finished). Reconcile = bounded re-read of /state every 50 ms for <=3 s BEFORE any fallback dispatch
phases.P7_live_fallback: N1 (Submit renamed) with the LIVE chooser as fallback (max 2 fallback decisions), n=3 subprocess cells, timed under the EXCLUSIVE lock

fallback_policy: At a failed precondition the CURRENT state goes to the chooser (never a restart at step 1): fresh semantic_v2 observation -> unmodified FixtureFormTask candidates -> drop any page candidate whose role+name is not unique in that observation -> chooser (mock or live) -> dispatch with that observation's ref -> completion candidates end with the bounded oracle re-read. At most 2 fallback decisions, then explicit stop.
replay_policy: Before every mutation: fresh semantic_v2 observation; unique role+name bind; preconditions (page_origin, field_state, declared action) and the dependency's postcondition (the field holds the token) checked on THAT observation; dispatch with the ref minted by it. Refusal (isError, status=refused or effect=refused) is not an effect; browser_ref_stale gets exactly one rebind from a fresh observation, any other refusal stops. A transport failure on a mutation is UNKNOWN: Submit -> reconcile by bounded re-read; type -> stop unknown. After the last step, bounded oracle re-read (10 ms cadence, <=3 s, R2-06). Unresolved stays unknown; nothing is replayed.

metrics.T: harness-side: monotonic send time of the first semantic_v2 get_browser_state of the trial -> first harness /state poll (4 ms cadence, header X-R207-Oracle so it is never journaled as a caller read) that shows submitted == token
metrics.T_target: secondary: first semantic_v2 send -> target journal applied event
metrics.process_wall: spawn -> exit of the caller process (includes Driver/Chrome start and teardown)
metrics.independent_oracle: the fixture's target-owned journal (received/applied per POST /submit, value compared to the trial token only) + /state; never the caller's report and never events
metrics.provider_receipts: per HTTP attempt: host, path, status, reached, request-id presence + sha256 prefix; per decision: backend, model, token usage, selected id. Never headers, bodies, typed text or the key

analysis.paired: per round d_CB = T(C)-T(B), d_CA = T(C)-T(A), d_BA = T(B)-T(A) over rounds where both arms are independently verified; median and 95% percentile bootstrap CI of the median (10000 resamples, seed 20261002, Python random). Failed trials are not imputed; they stay in the N-of-M denominators and the all-invocation costs
analysis.also_reported: per-arm median/IQR T, T_target, process_wall; T by position; provider decisions, tokens and requests deleted per warm run (work deleted) separately from paired T saved (wall-clock saved); stale window = observation end -> mutation dispatch start per arm

reported_separately: fallback (P7 T to explicit stop, wall, requests)
wrong-match (N8 routine time to stop, informational/untimed)
totals over ALL compiled-routine invocations incl. failures
costs.break_even: only if the measured median saving per warm replay vs B (and vs A) is > 0: incremental n* = ceil((compile_ms + admission T) / saving); conservative n* additionally counts the whole learning run T as overhead
costs.never: successful-replay-only latency is never presented as whole-workload latency

gates.G1: P1 learning run independently verified, 2 live decisions
gates.G2: P3 clean-reset replay independently verified before admission, 0 fallback, 0 provider requests
gates.G3: 100% of compiled-routine mutation dispatches (P3, P4-C, P5, P6, P7; fallback dispatches included) used a ref minted by the routine's latest observation, taken after the previous mutation
gates.G4: every routine negative row (N1-N8, 3/3 reps) ends verified or as an explicit stop with 0 stale dispatch, 0 ambiguous dispatch (dispatch on a non-unique role+name), 0 duplicate submit (journal applied <= 1); N8 dispatches nothing
gates.G5: P6 rows: reconcile read before any fallback dispatch, 0 duplicates (journal received <= 1, applied <= 1), 0 re-dispatch after an unknown mutation, resolved rows end verified_by_reconcile, unresolved stays unknown
gates.G6: costs above reported separately with all-invocation denominators

stale_dispatch_attribution.routine_attributable: a dispatch whose ref was not minted by the routine's latest observation taken after the previous mutation (G3 violation), or any re-dispatch of a possibly landed mutation
stale_dispatch_attribution.driver_accepted_stale_node: N4a: the Driver ACCEPTS a dispatch whose bound DOM node the page replaced after the routine's fresh observation. Counted and reported as a stale dispatch for G4 (so G4 fails if it occurs and KEEP is impossible). It is attributed to the Driver, not the routine, iff the N4a_ord comparator shows the same acceptance on the unmodified run.py path. The KILL rule's 'stale dispatch' is applied to routine-attributable stale dispatches; this split is a pre-registered deviation from the literal spec text, justified by the shakedown disclosure above. Readers who apply the literal rule should read the disposition as KILL; both readings are printed in the summary.

disposition_rules.KILL: any routine-attributable stale dispatch; any ambiguous dispatch; any duplicate submit in any phase; any unverified success (caller reports verified, journal disagrees); an authority field in the artifact; failed admission (P3); N8 dispatching anything; or the median paired T(C)-T(B) CI includes 0 or lies above 0
disposition_rules.KEEP: G1-G6 all hold, C faster than both B and A with CI upper bounds < 0, and C independently verified >= 19/20 with every C failure safe (explicit stop/unknown, no duplicate)
disposition_rules.REVISE: otherwise, with the measured narrowed claim stated

claim_boundary: one admitted #24 class (fill->submit), Python runner, trycua/cua PR 4316 merged onto main c4d0c6625, Driver 0.32.0 8b037961, TypeSafe model as reported in the receipts, feedback OFF, X11 Xvfb, Chrome 151. Not a routine framework; nothing transfers to other tasks. toggle->confirm and modal->act admission under the same schema is assessed at SOURCE/FIXTURE level only.
invariants: no routine engine, route miner, router, registry, batch API, second verifier or service; the compiled routine is packet harness code; refs, element tokens, capture ids, target/tab ids, session ids/epochs, backend node ids and coordinates never become stored authority; a possibly landed effect stays unknown until reconciled and is never blind-replayed; events are never the oracle
